1\. Explain the significance of the rights and duties of the faithful in relation to the "building up of the Body of Christ".

2\. What are the principal ways in which the faithful can cooperate in the bishop's task of governing the diocese?

**\**
**CHAPTER XVI:\
GROUPINGS OF ECCLESIASTICAL CIRCUMSCRIPTIONS\**

> READINGS FOR THIS CHAPTER
>
> [Code of Canon Law](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1dBfZuE0O4NTYPiaEdeUtdegdSEyK5YQM/view): Book II, canons 431-459.
>
> Vatican II, Decree concerning the Pastoral Office of Bishops in the Church [*Christus Dominus*](https://www.vatican.va/archive/hist_councils/ii_vatican_council/documents/vat-ii_decree_19651028_christus-dominus_en.html), 28 October 1965, nos. 37-38.
>
> John Paul II, Apostolic Letter *motu proprio* [*Apostolos Suos*](https://www.vatican.va/content/john-paul-ii/en/motu_proprio/documents/hf_jp-ii_motu-proprio_22071998_apostolos-suos.html), 21 May 1998.

**1. The pastoral function of supradiocesan structures**

The Second Vatican Council considered it "supremely fitting that everywhere bishops belonging to the same nation or region form an association which would meet at fixed times. Thus, when the insights of prudence and experience have been shared and views exchanged, there will emerge a holy union of energies in the service of the common good of the Churches" (Vatican II, Decree [*Christus Dominus*](https://www.vatican.va/archive/hist_councils/ii_vatican_council/documents/vat-ii_decree_19651028_christus-dominus_en.html), no. 37).

The supradiocesan unions that are formed in accordance with this suggestion of Vatican II are a manifestation of the collective exercise (by several bishops) of the pastoral task proper to the College of Bishops.

Although the law prescribes a certain number of matters in which the bishops may act collectively together (where uniformity is required for pastoral coordination), the bishop remains the one responsible in his own diocese, and retains all the power needed to govern it.

**2. Pastoral groupings of particular Churches into ecclesiastical provinces and regions**

**a) The ecclesiastical province**

"Neighbouring particular Churches are to be grouped into ecclesiastical provinces, with a certain defined territory. The purpose of this grouping is to promote, according to the circumstances of persons and place, a common pastoral action of various neighbouring dioceses, and the more closely to foster relations between diocesan bishops" (canon 431 §1).

> The wording of canon 431 §1 makes the establishment of the ecclesiastical province obligatory: see also canon 431 §2[^363].
>
> It is erected by the Roman Pontiff (canon 431 §3[^364]), and has juridical personality (canon 432 §2[^365]). It exercises power through the particular council (see below).

**b) The ecclesiastical region**

"If it seems advantageous, especially in countries where there are very many particular Churches, the Holy See can, on the proposal of the Episcopal Conference, join together neighbouring provinces into ecclesiastical regions" (canon 433 §1).

> The ecclesiastical region is thus a grouping of ecclesiastical provinces. Its establishment is discretionary. It is erected by the Holy See at the request of the Episcopal Conference.

**3. Juridical institutions of the ecclesiastical province**

**a) The Metropolitan Archbishop**

The Metropolitan Archbishop presides over the ecclesiastical province (canon 435[^366]). (The other dioceses in the province are called "suffragan" dioceses.)

The Metropolitan has responsibility for vigilance and for the other functions established by law or by special conferral on the part of the Holy See (canon 436[^367]).

**b) The particular council**

The particular council is meeting of the bishops of the Episcopal Conference or of the ecclesiastical province, to allow the collective exercise of their governmental function for the benefit of their respective particular Churches.

It can be a

- **plenary council** (a meeting of the particular Churches within an Episcopal Conference, convened with the approval of the Holy See: canons 439 §1[^368], 441[^369]); or a

- **provincial council** (a meeting of the particular Churches of a province, convened by the Metropolitan: canons 440[^370], 442[^371]).

> Canon 443[^372] gives details of the members of the council. Its functions -- principally legislative -- are set out in canon 445[^373].

**4. Juridical institutions at the national level: the Episcopal Conference**

> See [*Christus Dominus*](https://www.vatican.va/archive/hist_councils/ii_vatican_council/documents/vat-ii_decree_19651028_christus-dominus_en.html), nos. 37-38.

The Episcopal Conference is an assembly of bishops of a nation or of a specific territory, whose main role is that of pastoral coordination: cf. canon 447[^374]. The Apostolic Letter *motu proprio* [*Apostolos Suos*](https://www.vatican.va/content/john-paul-ii/en/motu_proprio/documents/hf_jp-ii_motu-proprio_22071998_apostolos-suos.html) of Pope John Paul II, 21 May 1998, deals at length with the theological and juridical nature of Episcopal Conferences, and sets out norms to complement the provisions of the Code of Canon Law.

As a rule the Episcopal Conference does not have juridical power, although it can issue general decrees in accordance with the conditions established by law: cf. canon 455[^375].

> A general decree has the force of law (canon 29[^376]). The Episcopal Conference's power to issue such decrees is limited to the matters specified by the Code, or for which it is given a special mandate by the Holy See. Outside of these matters, any general decrees it issues are null. Its general decrees must be passed by a two-thirds majority, and must be reviewed by the Holy See prior to promulgation.
>
> Canon 454[^377] determines who has the power to vote at plenary meetings of the Episcopal Conference.

? QUESTIONS

1\. What is the purpose of supradiocesan structures in the Church? Which of these structures are obligatory?

2\. What is the principal role of the Episcopal Conference?

**\**
**CHAPTER XVII:\
THE TEACHING OFFICE OF THE CHURCH\**

> READINGS FOR THIS CHAPTER
>
> [Code of Canon Law](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1dBfZuE0O4NTYPiaEdeUtdegdSEyK5YQM/view): Book III, canons 747-748, 822-832.
>
> Vatican II, Decree on the Media of Social Communications [*Inter Mirifica*](https://www.vatican.va/archive/hist_councils/ii_vatican_council/documents/vat-ii_decree_19631204_inter-mirifica_en.html), 4 December 1963.
>
> Vatican II, Decree on the Apostolate of the Laity [*Apostolicam Actuositatem*](https://www.vatican.va/archive/hist_councils/ii_vatican_council/documents/vat-ii_decree_19651118_apostolicam-actuositatem_en.html), 18 November 1965, no. 24.
>
> Vatican II, Decree on Religious Freedom [*Dignitatis Humanae*](https://www.vatican.va/archive/hist_councils/ii_vatican_council/documents/vat-ii_decl_19651207_dignitatis-humanae_en.html), 7 December 1965, no. 1.
>
> Vatican II, Pastoral Constitution on the Church in the Modern World [*Gaudium et Spes*](https://www.vatican.va/archive/hist_councils/ii_vatican_council/documents/vat-ii_const_19651207_gaudium-et-spes_en.html), 7 December 1965, no. 76.
>
> Congregation for the Doctrine of the Faith, [*Instruction on some Aspects of the Use of the Instruments of Social Communication in Promoting the Doctrine of the Faith*](https://www.vatican.va/roman_curia/congregations/cfaith/documents/rc_con_cfaith_doc_19920330_istruzione-pccs_en.html), 30 March 1992.
>
> [*Catechism of the Catholic Church*](https://www.vatican.va/archive/ENG0015/__P74.HTM), no. 2032.
>
> John Paul II, Apostolic Letter *motu proprio [Ad Tuendam Fidem](https://www.vatican.va/content/john-paul-ii/en/motu_proprio/documents/hf_jp-ii_motu-proprio_30061998_ad-tuendam-fidem.html)*, 18 May 1998.
>
> Pontifical Council for Social Communications, [*The Church and Internet*](https://www.vatican.va/roman_curia/pontifical_councils/pccs/documents/rc_pc_pccs_doc_20020228_church-internet_en.html), 22 February 2002.
>
> Pontifical Council for Social Communications, [*Ethics in Internet*](https://www.vatican.va/roman_curia/pontifical_councils/pccs/documents/rc_pc_pccs_doc_20020228_ethics-internet_en.html.), 22 February 2002.

**1. The juridical dimension of the teaching office ("*munus docendi*")**

The "*munus docendi*" involves a series of functions:

- receiving the Word;

- preserving the Word received and delving into it more deeply;

- transmitting the Word.

> Those who oppose the notion of law in the Church (see chapter I) would regard it as unacceptable to apply canon law to the Word of God, since -- as Martin Luther argued -- people who are free and subject only to the divine Word cannot be made prisoners of the words of men. However, if one accepts that rights and duties may arise in relation to the Word of God (every person has the right to receive the Word of God in all its authenticity), then it becomes clear that there is an intrinsic juridical dimension to that Word.

**2. Rights and duties of the faithful in receiving, preserving and transmitting the Word**

At baptism everyone becomes entitled to receive the message of a salvation in a continuous, progressive manner, suited to his or her needs.

The principal **right** of the faithful in this area is to receive the Word of God, and thereafter to maintain it, reflect upon it, and communicate it to others.

> Evangelisation needs to begin with those who are members of the Church, so that it can then reach others. The Vatican II Decree on Religious Freedom [*Dignitatis Humanae*](https://www.vatican.va/archive/hist_councils/ii_vatican_council/documents/vat-ii_decl_19651207_dignitatis-humanae_en.html), no. 1, makes clear that "truth can impose itself on the mind of man only in virtue of its own truth"; and canon 748 §2 states that "It is never lawful for anyone to force others to embrace the Catholic faith against their conscience".

The primary juridical **duty** of each one is to preserve communion in the faith with the other baptised members.

**3. The role of the hierarchy**

Communion in the faith is essentially hierarchical. The ecclesiastical authority is not merely an arbiter of good order. Rather, there is a particular responsibility on the Pastors in connection with the Word of God entrusted to the Church: "He who hears you, hears Me" (*Lk* 10:16).

The most obvious juridical consequences of this hierarchical dimension of the Word of God are

- the right of the faithful to receive the Word;

- the corresponding duty on the Pastors to provide the Word;

- the duty of the faithful to obey the ecclesiastical Magisterium.

It should also be borne in mind that the mission and power of the hierarchy are essentially a *service*, aimed at ensuring that each person, in whatever circumstance, may enter into true contact with the Gospel of Christ.

> It is the entire Church that possesses the truth. Therefore all the faithful have the right and duty of influencing temporal structures and evangelising (see next chapter). However, the evangelising function common to all the faithful does not have the *public* character which it does in the case of the hierarchy. The laity have an obligation to do apostolate, and teach others through example and word, but they cannot teach with authority.
>
> This shared responsibility means that should be no tension between the doctrinal authority of the Pastors, and the freedom of the faithful in accepting the Word.

**4. Judgements of the hierarchy on temporal matters**

"The Church has the right always and everywhere to proclaim moral principles, even in respect of the social order, and to make judgements about any human matter in so far as this is required by fundamental human rights or the salvation of souls": canon 747 §2.

> The Vatican II Pastoral Constitution on the Church in the Modern World [*Gaudium et Spes*](https://www.vatican.va/archive/hist_councils/ii_vatican_council/documents/vat-ii_const_19651207_gaudium-et-spes_en.html), no. 76, speaks of the Church's right to "true freedom to preach the faith, to teach her social doctrine, to exercise her role freely among men, and also to pass moral judgement in those matters which regard public order when the fundamental rights of a person or the salvation of souls require it." In so doing the Church fosters and elevates "all that is found to be true, good and beautiful in the human community \[and\] strengthens peace among men for the glory of God". See also Vatican II, Decree on the Apostolate of the Laity [*Apostolicam Actuositatem*](https://www.vatican.va/archive/hist_councils/ii_vatican_council/documents/vat-ii_decree_19651118_apostolicam-actuositatem_en.html), no. 24; [*Catechism of the Catholic Church*](https://www.vatican.va/archive/ENG0015/__P74.HTM), no. 2032.
>
> Note that the Church does not make "temporal judgements" but rather "judgements on temporal matters". There is a great difference between directing earthly affairs and ensuring that these are not an obstacle to the mission of the Church and the salvation of souls.

**5. Instruments of social communication: approval or permission for publishing books**

> See the Vatican II Decree on the Media of Social Communications [*Inter Mirifica*](https://www.vatican.va/archive/hist_councils/ii_vatican_council/documents/vat-ii_decree_19631204_inter-mirifica_en.html), 4 December 1963.

The Church has the right and duty to imbue with a Christian spirit the means of social communication, and to use and possess them in so far as they are necessary or useful for Christian education and for the salvation of souls. This is principally the responsibility of the laity, while the role of the Pastors is to remind everyone of their correct use and take steps to ensure that they help rather than hinder the task of evangelisation (see canon 822).

Canon 831 §1[^378] states that unless there is a just and reasonable cause, Catholics cannot write in newspapers and other publications which clearly are accustomed to attack religion or good customs. Clerics and members of religious institutes also need the permission of the local Ordinary.

The Episcopal Conference is to lay down norms regarding clerics and members of religious institutes taking part in radio and TV programmes concerning faith or morals (canon 831 §2[^379]).

> Concerning the implications of the Internet for religion and especially for the Catholic Church, see the document [*The Church and Internet*](https://www.vatican.va/roman_curia/pontifical_councils/pccs/documents/rc_pc_pccs_doc_20020228_church-internet_en.html), 22 February 2002, and a companion document of the same date [*Ethics in Internet*](https://www.vatican.va/roman_curia/pontifical_councils/pccs/documents/rc_pc_pccs_doc_20020228_ethics-internet_en.html.) (Pontifical Council for Social Communications).

Canon 823 §1[^380] refers to the Pastors' duty of vigilance concerning books relating to faith and morals.

> On the various approvals and permissions required for publications concerning Scripture, theology, canon law, Church history, religious or moral subjects, see canons 824-832[^381]. See also Congregation for the Doctrine of the Faith, [*Instruction on some Aspects of the Use of the Instruments of Social Communication in Promoting the Doctrine of the Faith*](https://www.vatican.va/roman_curia/congregations/cfaith/documents/rc_con_cfaith_doc_19920330_istruzione-pccs_en.html), 30 March 1992.

**6. Profession of faith**

> See canon 833[^382], which lists the situations in which a profession of faith is required.

In 1967 the Sacred Congregation for the Doctrine of the Faith published a formula which was updated in 1989 and which incorporated an oath of fidelity. This was further amended to take into account the three levels of truth in the *motu proprio [Ad Tuendam Fidem](https://www.vatican.va/content/john-paul-ii/en/motu_proprio/documents/hf_jp-ii_motu-proprio_30061998_ad-tuendam-fidem.html)* of 18 May 1998 (see next chapter).

1\. In what ways do the faithful of the Church share responsibility with the hierarchy for evangelisation?

2\. What role do the laity have in relation to the means of social communication?

**CHAPTER XVIII:\
THE MINISTRY OF THE WORD\**

> READINGS FOR THIS CHAPTER
