**1. The sacrament of the Eucharist and the mystery of the Church**

Canon 897[^487] provides the doctrinal framework for the norms on the Eucharist, and sets out the essential aspects of the Catholic faith concerning the Eucharistic mystery:

- the blessed Eucharist is the most august sacrament since in it Christ the Lord himself is *contained* (Real Presence), *offered* (Sacrifice) and *received* (Communion);

- by the Eucharist the Church lives and grows continually (see John Paul's Encyclical [*Ecclesia de Eucharistia*](https://www.vatican.va/content/john-paul-ii/en/encyclicals/documents/hf_jp-ii_enc_20030417_eccl-de-euch.html), 17 April 2003);

- in the Eucharistic Sacrifice, the memorial of the death and resurrection of the Lord, the Sacrifice of the Cross is for ever perpetuated (see the [*Catechism of the Catholic Church*](https://www.vatican.va/archive/ENG0015/__P41.HTM), nos. 1362-1368);

- the Eucharistic Sacrifice is the summit and source of all worship and Christian life; to it are directed all the other sacraments and all ecclesiastical ministries and works of the apostolate (see the [*Catechism of the Catholic Church*](https://www.vatican.va/archive/ENG0015/__P3X.HTM), nos. 1324-1327);

- by means of the Eucharistic Sacrifice the unity of God's people is signified and brought about, and the building up of the body of Christ is perfected;

- as a result, no Christian community can be built up unless it is rooted in and revolves around the blessed Eucharist, as the Code makes clear in several places.

**2. Triple aspect of the Holy Eucharist**

The Eucharistic celebration is at once both a Sacrifice and Communion. "In it, Christ the Lord, through the ministry of the priest", acting *in persona Christi*, "offers himself, substantially present under the appearance of bread and wine, to God the Father", thus perpetuating the Sacrifice of the Cross, "and gives himself as spiritual nourishment to the faithful who are associated with him in his offering" (canon 899[^488]).

Catholic teaching on the Eucharist embraces these various essential dimensions of the sacrament, so that "it is not permissible for us, in thought, life or action, to take away from this truly most holy Sacrament its full magnitude and its essential meaning. It is at one and the same time a Sacrifice-Sacrament, a Communion-Sacrament and a Presence-Sacrament. And although it is true that the Eucharist always was and must continue to be the most profound revelation of the human brotherhood of Christ's disciples and confessors, it cannot be treated merely as an 'occasion' for manifesting this brotherhood. When celebrating the Sacrament of the Body and Blood of the Lord, the full magnitude of the divine mystery must be respected, as must the full meaning of this sacramental sign" (John Paul II, Encyclical [*Redemptor Hominis*](https://www.vatican.va/content/john-paul-ii/en/encyclicals/documents/hf_jp-ii_enc_04031979_redemptor-hominis.html), no. 20).

In conformity with this teaching, the obligation of the faithful to give maximum veneration to the blessed Eucharist is made specific in three ways (canon 898[^489]):

- taking an active part in the celebration of the most august Sacrifice;

- receiving the sacrament with great devotion and frequently;

- reverencing it with the greatest adoration.

> NB: although the Eucharistic celebration is an action of the whole Church in which the common priesthood and the ministerial priesthood operate, these forms of participating in Christ's priesthood are *essentially* different: "the celebrant, as minister of this sacrifice, is the authentic *priest*, performing -- in virtue of the specific power of sacred Ordination -- a true sacrificial act that brings creation back to God. Although all those who participate in the Eucharist do not confect the sacrifice as he does, they offer with him, by virtue of the common priesthood, their own *spiritual sacrifices* represented by the bread and wine from the moment of their presentation at the altar" (John Paul II, Letter [*Dominicae Cenae*](https://www.vatican.va/content/john-paul-ii/en/letters/1980/documents/hf_jp-ii_let_19800224_dominicae-cenae.html), 24 February 1980, no. 9).

**3. Sacrifice-Sacrament: the Holy Mass**

**a) The celebration of the Eucharist as an action of Christ and the Church**

> See the [*Catechism of the Catholic Church*](https://www.vatican.va/archive/ENG0015/__P41.HTM), nos. 1362-1372.

The Eucharistic celebration, even when the faithful cannot be present, is always an action of Christ and the Church (see canon 904[^490]):

- it is an action of Christ, because Christ is present in a real, operative way, both in the minister who acts *in persona Christi*, and above all under the Eucharistic species or in the Sacrifice offered to the Father, which is the very Sacrifice of Christ on the Cross;

- it is an action of the Church, because Christ acts through the Church's mediation, especially through the ministry of the priest, and also because the whole Church, pilgrim and heavenly, is involved in the celebration: in it "we are most closely united to the worship of the heavenly Church" (Dogmatic Constitution [*Lumen Gentium*](https://www.vatican.va/archive/hist_councils/ii_vatican_council/documents/vat-ii_const_19641121_lumen-gentium_en.html), no. 50), entering into true communion with the Saints.

**b) The minister of the Eucharistic Sacrifice**

> The Sacrament-Sacrifice, Sacrament-Communion and Sacrament-Presence dimensions normally take place within the same Eucharistic celebration, but can be the object of different liturgical activities. Even within the Mass, the sacrificial aspect is different from the administration of Communion. The norms on the Eucharistic minister reflect this triple dimension.

"The only minister who, in the person of Christ, can bring into being the sacrament of the Eucharist, is a validly ordained priest" (canon 900 §1): this is a canonical formulation of divine law.

Acting *in persona Christi* means more than acting "in the name of" or "in the place of" Christ. "*In persona* means in specific sacramental identification with the eternal High Priest who is the Author and principal Subject of this Sacrifice of his, a Sacrifice in which, in truth, nobody can take his place" (John Paul II, [*Dominicae Cenae*](https://www.vatican.va/content/john-paul-ii/en/letters/1980/documents/hf_jp-ii_let_19800224_dominicae-cenae.html), no. 8).

> See the Instruction [*Redemptionis Sacramentum*](https://www.vatican.va/roman_curia/congregations/ccdds/documents/rc_con_ccdds_doc_20040423_redemptionis-sacramentum_en.html), 25 March 2004, nos. 30, 147.

**c) Requisites for the valid and lawful confection of the sacrament of the Eucharist**

The validity of the celebration of the Eucharist is dependent on the valid ordination of the priest (canon 1024[^491]). The celebration of the Eucharist is proper and exclusive to the ministerial priesthood.

> Simulation of the Mass is expressly condemned in canon 1379 §1, 1º [^492]. The Apostolic Letter *motu proprio [Sacramentorum Sanctitatis Tutela](https://www.vatican.va/roman_curia/congregations/cfaith/documents/rc_con_cfaith_doc_20211011_norme-delittiriservati-cfaith_en.html)* (2021 revision), art. 3, includes it among the "more serious offences" ("*graviora delicta*").

The lawfulness of the celebration depends on two factors:

- the minister should not be impeded by canon law, owing to some irregularity or impediment to his ordination (see canon 1044[^493]);

- he should also be in a state of grace unless there is a grave reason for celebrating Mass and no opportunity to confess (see canon 916[^494]; [*Catechism of the Catholic Church*](https://www.vatican.va/archive/ENG0015/__P4D.HTM), no. 1457).

By divine institution, bread and wine are the necessary and indispensable matter. Bread must be wheaten, and recently made (if it loses its qualities it ceases to be valid matter); wine must be natural, from grapes of the vine, and not corrupt (see canon 924[^495]; [*Catechism of the Catholic Church*](https://www.vatican.va/archive/ENG0015/__P3Z.HTM), nos. 1333-1336. See also the Instruction [*Redemptionis Sacramentum*](https://www.vatican.va/roman_curia/congregations/ccdds/documents/rc_con_ccdds_doc_20040423_redemptionis-sacramentum_en.html), 25 March 2004, nos. 48-50, on "The Matter of the Most Holy Eucharist").

For lawfulness, in the Latin Church, unleavened bread must be used (canon 926[^496]). Also, a small quantity of water must be added to the wine (canon 924 §1).

> See the 2003 [norms](https://www.vatican.va/roman_curia/congregations/cfaith/documents/rc_con_cfaith_doc_20030724_pane-senza-glutine_en.html#:~:text=Common%20Norms-,1.,occasioned%20the%20granting%20of%20permission.) of the Congregation \[now Dicastery\] for the Doctrine of the Faith on the use of gluten-free hosts and mustum (fresh juice from a ripe grape or juice preserved by methods that suspend its fermentation, e.g. by freezing). Completely gluten-free hosts are invalid matter; true mustum is valid matter for the Eucharist. Commercially available grape juice is, for the most part, invalid matter. See also Congregation \[now Dicastery\] for Divine Worship and the Discipline of the Sacraments, [*Circular letter to Bishops on the bread and wine for the Eucharist*](https://www.vatican.va/roman_curia/congregations/ccdds/documents/rc_con_ccdds_doc_20170615_lettera-su-pane-vino-eucaristia_en.html), 15 June 2017.

"It is absolutely wrong, even in urgent and extreme necessity, to consecrate one element without the other, or even to consecrate both outside the Eucharistic celebration" (canon 927[^497]).

> Not even the Pope can dispense from this prohibition, because it affects the very essence of the sacrament. This offence is one of the *graviora delicta* in [*Sacramentorum Sanctitatis Tutela*](https://www.vatican.va/roman_curia/congregations/cfaith/documents/rc_con_cfaith_doc_20211011_norme-delittiriservati-cfaith_en.html).
>
> See canons 901-909[^498] for other norms concerning the celebration itself. Regarding the time and place of the celebration, see canons 931-933[^499].\
> \
> The Apostolic Letter *motu proprio [Summorum Pontificum](https://www.vatican.va/content/benedict-xvi/en/motu_proprio/documents/hf_ben-xvi_motu-proprio_20070707_summorum-pontificum.html)*, 7 July 2007, and the Pontifical Commission *Ecclesia Dei*'s Instruction [*Universae Ecclesiae*](https://www.vatican.va/roman_curia/pontifical_commissions/ecclsdei/documents/rc_com_ecclsdei_doc_20110430_istr-universae-ecclesiae_en.html), 30 April 2011, specify the circumstances in which Mass may be celebrated according to the Missal promulgated by John XXIII in 1962 (the "Extraordinary Form"). These have now been largely overruled by Pope Francis's *motu proprio [Traditionis custodes](https://www.vatican.va/content/francesco/en/motu_proprio/documents/20210716-motu-proprio-traditionis-custodes.html)* of 16 July 2021.
>
> Canons 945-958[^500] deal with the question of Mass offerings or stipends. They include detailed provisions to ensure that there is not even the tiniest suspicion of trafficking, which in fact constitutes a specific crime (see canon 1383[^501]). In any event, priests are earnestly recommended, even if they do not receive a stipend, to celebrate Mass for the intentions of Christ's faithful, especially those in need (see canon 945 §2[^502]).

**4. Communion-Sacrament**

**a) The minister of Communion**

Canon 910 §1 establishes that: "The ordinary minister of holy communion is a bishop, a priest or a deacon".

> Pope John Paul II, in [*Dominicae Cenae*](https://www.vatican.va/content/john-paul-ii/en/letters/1980/documents/hf_jp-ii_let_19800224_dominicae-cenae.html), no. 11, states that, as ministers of the Holy Eucharist, priests have primary responsibility for the sacred species, having been "consecrated by their ordination to represent Christ the Priest: for this reason their hands, like their words and their will, have become direct instruments of Christ ... To touch the sacred species and to distribute them with their own hands is a privilege of the ordained, one which indicates an active participation in the ministry of the Eucharist. It is obvious that the Church can grant this faculty to those who are neither priests nor deacons \... but always after an adequate preparation".

Canon 910 §2[^503] refers to extraordinary ministers -- male or female -- of Holy Communion: first of all the acolyte (see canon 230 §1[^504]), who needs no special designation as an extraordinary minister, but who nevertheless acts only "extraordinarily", that is, when the ordinary minister is absent or impeded. Other laity can be extraordinary ministers, provided the conditions in canon 230 §3[^505] are fulfilled: i.e. the needs of the Church so require, and ordinary ministers are not available.

> The Instruction [*Redemptionis Sacramentum*](https://www.vatican.va/roman_curia/congregations/ccdds/documents/rc_con_ccdds_doc_20040423_redemptionis-sacramentum_en.html) (nos. 156-160) identifies and corrects certain abuses in this regard. See also the Holy See's [*Instruction on* *Certain Questions Regarding the Collaboration of the Non-Ordained Faithful in the Sacred Ministry of the Priest*](https://www.vatican.va/roman_curia/congregations/cclergy/documents/rc_con_interdic_doc_15081997_en.html), 15 August 1997, art. 8 §2.

**b) Requisites for the lawful administration and reception of the sacrament**

All the faithful have the fundamental right to receive from the sacred Pastors the spiritual goods of the Church, principally the word of God and the sacraments (canon 213[^506]; see the [*Catechism of the Catholic Church*](https://www.vatican.va/archive/ENG0015/__P74.HTM), no. 2037). Consequently, the sacraments cannot be denied to those who opportunely ask for them, and are properly disposed and not prohibited by law (canon 843[^507]). These norms are sufficient in themselves, but the legislator has wished to stress the right in relation to the Eucharist: any baptised person who is not forbidden by law may and must be admitted to Communion (canon 912[^508]); and it is for each one to judge whether in the particular case he or she is able to receive the Body of our Lord (see canon 916[^509]).

The connection between Sacrifice and banquet makes it desirable that Communion be received within the Eucharistic celebration, but it can be received outside Mass for a good reason (canon 918[^510]).

Canon 915[^511] forbids those under penalty of excommunication or interdict, and those who obstinately persist in manifest grave sin, to receive Communion.

> The post-synodal Apostolic Exhortation [*Familiaris Consortio*](https://www.vatican.va/content/john-paul-ii/en/apost_exhortations/documents/hf_jp-ii_exh_19811122_familiaris-consortio.html), 22 November 1981, deals with the question of divorced and remarried Catholics and whether they can be readmitted to Communion (nos. 82, 84). See also Pope Benedict XVI's post-synodal Apostolic Exhortation [*Sacramentum Caritatis*](https://www.vatican.va/content/benedict-xvi/en/apost_exhortations/documents/hf_ben-xvi_exh_20070222_sacramentum-caritatis.html), 22 February 2007, no. 29, on "The Eucharist and the indissolubility of marriage".
>
> It is the parish priest who discerns in these cases, acting with due pastoral charity and prudence, and bearing in mind what Pope Francis says in [*Amoris Laetitia*](https://www.vatican.va/content/dam/francesco/pdf/apost_exhortations/documents/papa-francesco_esortazione-ap_20160319_amoris-laetitia_en.pdf), no. 297: "It is a matter of reaching out to everyone, of needing to help each person find his or her proper way of participating in the ecclesial community and thus to experience being touched by an 'unmerited, unconditional and gratuitous' mercy."
>
> Canons 917-923[^512] deal with

- reception of the Eucharist more than once on the same day (the Holy See has subsequently clarified that Communion can be received only once more on the same day, within Mass);

- receiving Communion outside Mass;

- the Eucharistic fast;

- the annual obligation to receive Communion;

- Viaticum;

- the possibility of receiving Communion in any Catholic rite.

**c) First Communion of children**

Lack of age and of due preparation are limitations which the law places on the right to receive Communion. Normally two conditions have to be fulfilled before Communion can be given to children: use of reason or sufficient knowledge, and careful preparation, so that according to their capacity they understand what the mystery of Christ means, and are able to receive the Body of the Lord with faith and devotion (canon 913 §1[^513]).

Given that the child should confess first (canon 914[^514]; [*Catechism of the Catholic Church*](https://www.vatican.va/archive/ENG0015/__P4D.HTM), no. 1457), this preparation also implies the formation of the moral conscience of the child.

In danger of death, it is sufficient that the child be able to distinguish the Body of Christ from ordinary food and receive it with reverence (canon 913 §2[^515]).

Once the child has attained the use of reason, it is primarily the duty of parents and the parish priest to ensure that the child is properly prepared in order to be able to receive Communion as soon as possible. The priest should also take care that those who are not prepared should not come to Communion (canon 914[^516]).

**d) Communion under both kinds**

The Second Vatican Council (Constitution on the Sacred Liturgy [*Sacrosanctum Concilium*](https://www.vatican.va/archive/hist_councils/ii_vatican_council/documents/vat-ii_const_19631204_sacrosanctum-concilium_en.html), no. 55) allowed Communion under both kinds in certain circumstances, the dogmatic principles laid down by the Council of Trent remaining intact. According to those principles, the whole and entire Christ and the true sacrament is received under either kind. Therefore there is no greater fullness of participation when both kinds are received. What is fuller is the *sign*, which is what justifies the increased possibility of receiving Communion under both kinds

If Communion is given under one kind, the species is that of bread. In case of necessity it can, with the bishop's permission, be given under the species of wine alone (e.g. for those with gluten intolerance).

> The cases in which Communion can be administered under both kinds are listed in the [*General Instruction of the Roman Missal*](https://www.liturgyoffice.org.uk/Resources/GIRM/Documents/GIRM.pdf), no. 283.

**5. Presence-Sacrament**

**a) Exposition and Benediction with the Blessed Sacrament**

"Adoration of Christ in this Sacrament of love must also find expression in various forms of Eucharistic devotion: personal prayer before the Blessed Sacrament, hours of adoration, periods of exposition -- short, prolonged and annual (Forty Hours) -- Eucharistic benediction, Eucharistic processions, Eucharistic Congresses. A particular mention should be made at this point of the Solemnity of the Body and Blood of Christ as an act of public worship rendered to Christ present in the Eucharist, a feast instituted by my predecessor Urban IV in memory of the institution of this great Mystery" (Pope John Paul II, Letter [*Dominicae Cenae*](https://www.vatican.va/content/john-paul-ii/en/letters/1980/documents/hf_jp-ii_let_19800224_dominicae-cenae.html), no. 3).

These forms of Eucharistic worship find positive endorsement in canons 941-944[^517].

> Benediction with either pyx (ciborium) or monstrance can take place on any day in any church or oratory which is allowed to reserve the Eucharist (canon 944). During exposition, celebration of the Mass in the body of the church is prohibited.

**b) The minister of Eucharistic Exposition and Benediction**

The minister of exposition and benediction is the priest or deacon, but in special circumstances the minister of exposition and deposition alone, without the blessing, is the acolyte, the extraordinary minister of Holy Communion, or another person deputed by the local Ordinary (canon 943).

? QUESTIONS

1\. What are the main doctrinal principles underpinning the Church's legislation on the Blessed Eucharist?

2\. Who are the ordinary ministers of the Eucharistic Sacrifice, of Holy Communion, and of Eucharistic Exposition and Benediction?

3\. In what circumstances may an extraordinary minister of Holy Communion administer the sacrament?

> Congregation for Divine Worship and the Discipline of the Sacraments, Instruction [*Redemptionis Sacramentum*](https://www.vatican.va/roman_curia/congregations/ccdds/documents/rc_con_ccdds_doc_20040423_redemptionis-sacramentum_en.html), 25 March 2004, no. 76.
>
> Benedict XVI, post-synodal Apostolic Exhortation [*Sacramentum Caritatis*](https://www.vatican.va/content/benedict-xvi/en/apost_exhortations/documents/hf_ben-xvi_exh_20070222_sacramentum-caritatis.html), 22 February 2007, no. 21.
>
> Apostolic Penitentiary, [*Note on the importance of the internal forum and the inviolability of the sacramental seal*](https://www.vatican.va/roman_curia/tribunals/apost_penit/documents/rc_trib_appen_pro_20190629_forointerno_en.html), 29 June 2019.
>
> Apostolic Letter *motu proprio* [*Sacramentorum Sanctitatis Tutela*](https://www.vatican.va/roman_curia/congregations/cfaith/documents/rc_con_cfaith_doc_20211011_norme-delittiriservati-cfaith_en.html), 2021 revision.

**1. Nature and effects of the sacrament of penance**

> See the [*Catechism of the Catholic Church*](https://www.vatican.va/archive/ENG0015/__P4C.HTM), nos. 1440-1470.

Christ instituted the sacrament of penance so that those falling into sin after baptism might "obtain pardon from God's mercy for the offence committed" and at the same time be "reconciled with the Church which they have wounded by their sins" (Dogmatic Constitution [*Lumen Gentium*](https://www.vatican.va/archive/hist_councils/ii_vatican_council/documents/vat-ii_const_19641121_lumen-gentium_en.html), no. 11).

Like the other sacraments, penance is an efficacious sign of grace: of pardon and reconciliation, which bring with them sanctifying grace for the penitent.

In penance the acts of the penitent form an essential part of the sacramental sign, so that without them there is no sacrament (just as there is no sacrament if there is no absolution).

These acts are:

- **contrition**; even if imperfect (**attrition**);

- **confession** of sins, preceded by an examination of conscience;

- **absolution** given by the priest;

- **satisfaction**.

The sacrament is a kind of *judicial act*, but the tribunal is one of mercy rather than of strict justice. By means of the absolution, the Church gives a visible judgement on the Christian penitent, which becomes a sign of the invisible judgement of God: an *efficacious* sign, because what is bound or loosed on earth is bound or loosed in heaven.

The sacrament is also medicinal: by it the penitent receives health of soul.

**2. The right to receive the sacrament**

According to [*Reconcilatio et Paenitentia*](https://www.vatican.va/content/john-paul-ii/en/apost_exhortations/documents/hf_jp-ii_exh_02121984_reconciliatio-et-paenitentia.html), no. 33, integral and individual confession of sins is an *inviolable* and *inalienable* right of the faithful.

> It is not a right as against divine mercy, but a right as before the ministers to receive sacramental forgiveness of sins committed after baptism, and the corresponding duty on pastors to make it possible and easy for the faithful to exercise this right and satisfy the needs of their souls.
>
> In this regard the law gives wide faculties to priests in cases of danger of death (see canon 976[^518]). Canon 986[^519] imposes an obligation on priests to offer a reasonable timetable for confessions. "All priests should dedicate themselves with generosity, commitment and competency to administering the sacrament of Reconciliation": Pope Benedict XVI, post-synodal Apostolic Exhortation [*Sacramentum Caritatis*](https://www.vatican.va/content/benedict-xvi/en/apost_exhortations/documents/hf_ben-xvi_exh_20070222_sacramentum-caritatis.html), no. 21.

**3. Individual and integral confession as a requirement of divine law**

"Individual and integral confession and absolution constitute the sole ordinary means by which a member of the faithful who is conscious of grave sin is reconciled with God and the Church. Physical or moral impossibility alone excuses from such confession, in which case reconciliation may be attained by other means also" (canon 960[^520]).

> Divine mercy is not bound to the sacramental sign, but individual confession is the ordinary means for obtaining pardon and reconciliation.
>
> "Physical impossibility" may be severe illness, lack of time before a grave danger, impossibility of speaking, etc.
>
> "Moral impossibility" may arise out of respect for the sacramental seal, or the danger of scandal or sin on the part of the penitent or of the confessor.
>
> Once the circumstances giving rise to the impossibility have disappeared, the obligation re-arises of confessing those serious sins which were not confessed (canon 988 §1[^521]).

**4. Circumstances in which collective absolution may be given**

> The relevant norms are to be found in canons 961-963[^522] and 988[^523] of the Code of Canon Law. See also John Paul II's Apostolic Letter *motu proprio* [*Misericordia Dei*](https://www.vatican.va/content/john-paul-ii/en/motu_proprio/documents/hf_jp-ii_motu-proprio_20020502_misericordia-dei.html), 7 April 2002.

Canon 961 §1 sets out the conditions for collective absolution as either:

- danger of death with no time for individual confessions (1º); or

- a combination of insufficient confessors, and circumstances whereby the penitents would be deprived for a lengthy time of sacramental grace or of Holy Communion (2º).

A gathering of a great number of penitents is not in itself sufficient to justify collective absolution.

For the validity of such an absolution, the penitent must be properly disposed, and also at the same time personally resolved to confess in due time each of the grave sins which cannot for the moment be so confessed (canons 962 §1, 963). The priest should make this clear, and should invite each person to make an act of contrition, if there is time, before the general absolution (canon 962 §2).

> "I ask pastors to be vigilant with regard to the celebration of the sacrament of Reconciliation, and to limit the practice of general absolution exclusively to the cases permitted, since individual absolution is the only form intended for ordinary use": Pope Benedict XVI, [*Sacramentum Caritatis*](https://www.vatican.va/content/benedict-xvi/en/apost_exhortations/documents/hf_ben-xvi_exh_20070222_sacramentum-caritatis.html), no. 21.

**5. The minister of the sacrament of penance**

> See the [*Catechism of the Catholic Church*](https://www.vatican.va/archive/ENG0015/__P4E.HTM), nos. 1461-1467.

Only a priest is a minister of the sacrament (canon 965[^524]), but in addition to the power of order, he also needs the faculty to exercise that power in respect of the faithful to whom he gives absolution (canon 966 §1).

> Details of how the faculty can be acquired are given in canons 966-975[^525].
>
> The supplying of jurisdiction established in canon 144 §1[^526] applies to the faculty for hearing confessions, in cases of common error of fact or law, and of positive doubt of fact and law (see above, chapter X, 4).
>
> The sacramental seal is absolutely inviolable (canons 983 §1[^527]; 1386[^528]; see also the [*Note of the Apostolic Penitentiary on the importance of the internal forum and the inviolability of the sacramental seal*](https://www.vatican.va/roman_curia/tribunals/apost_penit/documents/rc_trib_appen_pro_20190629_forointerno_en.html), 29 June 2019. The Apostolic Letter *motu proprio [Sacramentorum Sanctitatis Tutela](https://www.vatican.va/roman_curia/congregations/cfaith/documents/rc_con_cfaith_doc_20211011_norme-delittiriservati-cfaith_en.html)* (2021 revision) includes violation of the seal of confession among the "more serious offences" (*graviora delicta*).

**6. The place for hearing confession**

The proper place for hearing confessions is a church or oratory (canon 964 §1[^529]).

For the confessional, norms are to be provided by the Episcopal Conference, although confessionals with a fixed grille between the confessor and the penitent must always be available in an open place, for those who wish (canon 964 §2[^530]).

> Priests other than those celebrating Mass can hear the confessions of the faithful who so desire, even in the same place where Mass is being celebrated: see the Instruction [*Redemptionis Sacramentum*](https://www.vatican.va/roman_curia/congregations/ccdds/documents/rc_con_ccdds_doc_20040423_redemptionis-sacramentum_en.html), 25 March 2004, no. 76.

**7. Obligations of the penitent**

Penitents "must be so disposed that, repudiating the sins they have committed and having the purpose of amending their lives, they turn back to God" (canon 987[^531]).

Canon 988[^532] stipulates that each one is "bound to confess, in kind and number, all grave sins committed after baptism, of which after careful examination of conscience he or she is aware, which have not yet been directly pardoned by the keys of the Church, and which have not been confessed in an individual confession."

> Canon 916[^533] refers to the obligation to confess grave sins before celebrating Mass or receiving Communion. Canon 989[^534] sets out the obligation to confess one's grave sins at least once a year.
>
> Canon 988 §2 recommends the confession of venial sins. The sacrament of penance "is not only an instrument directed to destroy sin -- the negative aspect -- but also a valuable exercise of virtue which is itself expiation, an irreplaceable school of spirituality, a profoundly positive process of regeneration in the soul of the 'perfect man, fully mature with the fullness of Christ' (cf. *Eph* 4:13). In this sense confession which is rightly carried out is already in itself a very lofty form of spiritual direction. Precisely for these reasons the scope of utilisation of the sacrament of reconciliation cannot be reduced to a mere hypothesis of serious sin: apart from considerations of a dogmatic character which could be made in this regard, we call to mind that confession made at intervals, the so-called confession 'of devotion', has always accompanied the ascent to holiness in the Church" (John Paul II, [*Allocution 30 January 1981*](https://www.vatican.va/content/john-paul-ii/es/speeches/1981/january/documents/hf_jp-ii_spe_19810130_penitenzieri-roma.html); see the [*Catechism of the Catholic Church*](https://www.vatican.va/archive/ENG0015/__P4D.HTM), no. 1458)

**8. Indulgences**

"An indulgence is the remission in the sight of God of the temporal punishment due for sins, the guilt of which has already been forgiven. A member of Christ's faithful who is properly disposed and who fulfils certain specific conditions, may gain an indulgence by the help of the Church which, as the minister of redemption, authoritatively dispenses and applies the treasury of the merits of Christ and the Saints" (canon 992).

The 1983 Code deals only with the general law on indulgences, referring the rest to special laws of the Church, specifically the 1999 [*Enchiridion Indulgentiarum*](https://www.vatican.va/roman_curia/tribunals/apost_penit/documents/rc_trib_appen_doc_20020826_enchiridion-indulgentiarum_lt.html) of the Apostolic Penitentiary; see also the [*Catechism of the Catholic Church*](https://www.vatican.va/archive/ENG0015/__P4G.HTM), nos. 1471-1479.

? QUESTIONS

1\. What are the main rights and duties of the faithful in respect of the sacrament of penance?

2\. When may it be lawful to administer collective absolution?

**\**
**CHAPTER XXV:\
THE SACRAMENT OF ANOINTING OF THE SICK\**

> READINGS FOR THIS CHAPTER
>
> [Code of Canon Law](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1dBfZuE0O4NTYPiaEdeUtdegdSEyK5YQM/view): Book IV, canons 998-1007.
>
> Vatican II, Constitution on the Sacred Liturgy [*Sacrosanctum Concilium*](https://www.vatican.va/archive/hist_councils/ii_vatican_council/documents/vat-ii_const_19631204_sacrosanctum-concilium_en.html), 4 December 1963, no. 73.
>
> Vatican II, Dogmatic Constitution on the Church [*Lumen Gentium*](https://www.vatican.va/archive/hist_councils/ii_vatican_council/documents/vat-ii_const_19641121_lumen-gentium_en.html), 21 November 1964, no. 11.
>
> Paul VI, Apostolic Constitution [*Sacram Unctionem Infirmorum*](https://www.vatican.va/content/paul-vi/en/apost_constitutions/documents/hf_p-vi_apc_19721130_sacram-unctionem.html), 30 November 1972.
>
> [*Catechism of the Catholic Church*](https://www.vatican.va/archive/ENG0015/__P4J.HTM), nos. 1499-1532.
>
> Dicastery for the Doctrine of the Faith, [*Note on the Minister of the Sacrament of the Anointing of the Sick*](https://www.vatican.va/roman_curia/congregations/cfaith/documents/rc_con_cfaith_doc_20050211_unzione-infermi_en.html#:~:text=The%20doctrine%20which%20holds%20that,layman%20attempts%20to%20administer%20it.), 11 February 2005.

**1. Nature and effects of this sacrament**

In keeping with the desire of Vatican II (Constitution on the Sacred Liturgy [*Sacrosanctum Concilium*](https://www.vatican.va/archive/hist_councils/ii_vatican_council/documents/vat-ii_const_19631204_sacrosanctum-concilium_en.html), no. 73) the Instruction [*Inter Oecumenici*](https://adoremus.org/1964/09/inter-oecumenici/) of the Sacred Congregation of Rites, 26 September 1964, introduced the term "anointing of the sick" to replace that of "extreme unction", so as to make clear that "it is not a sacrament for those only who are at the point of death", and that "as soon as anyone of the faithful begins to be in danger of death from sickness or old age, the fitting time for that person to receive this sacrament has certainly already arrived".

Canon 998 states: "The anointing of the sick, by which the Church commends to the suffering and glorified Lord the faithful who are dangerously ill so that he may support and save them, is conferred by anointing them with oil and pronouncing the words prescribed in the liturgical books."

**2. The celebration of the sacrament**

The words of canon 998, taken from the Dogmatic Constitution [*Lumen Gentium*](https://www.vatican.va/archive/hist_councils/ii_vatican_council/documents/vat-ii_const_19641121_lumen-gentium_en.html), no. 11, indicate the object of the sacrament, and at the same time define the **matter** (the anointing with the holy oil), and **form** (the prescribed words: "Through this holy anointing may the Lord in his love and mercy help you with the grace of the Holy Spirit. May the Lord who frees you from sin save you and raise you up").

> The matter and form were definitively regulated by the 1972 Apostolic Constitution [*Sacram Unctionem Infirmorum*](https://www.vatican.va/content/paul-vi/en/apost_constitutions/documents/hf_p-vi_apc_19721130_sacram-unctionem.html). The oil to be used is olive oil, or in case of necessity some other vegetable oil. The oil can be blessed not only by a bishop (this is usually done in the Chrism Mass), but also by those equivalent to a diocesan bishop (see canons 381 §2[^535] and 368[^536]); and in case of necessity any priest, but only in the actual celebration of the sacrament.

Canon 1000[^537] establishes that anointings are to be carried out according to the liturgical books, which prescribe, for lawfulness, anointing of the forehead and hands.

> A single anointing is sufficient for validity, which need not necessarily be on the forehead.

It is up to relatives and the parish priest to see that the sacrament is provided (canon 1001[^538]). They should ensure a sound knowledge of the nature of the sacrament so that when the moment comes, it is the sick or elderly person who requests it. They should also avoid unnecessary delay, so that the person to be anointed may receive the sacrament with full faith and devotion, and in full possession of his or her faculties.

> Any communal celebration of the sacrament (see canon 1002[^539]) should not be detrimental to the necessary care and diligence in preparing for and administering the sacrament.

**3. The minister of the sacrament**

"Every priest, but only a priest, can validly administer the sacrament" (canon 1003 §1).

> On 11 February 2005 the Congregation for the Doctrine of the Faith issued a "[Note](https://www.vatican.va/roman_curia/congregations/cfaith/documents/rc_con_cfaith_doc_20050211_unzione-infermi_en.html#:~:text=The%20doctrine%20which%20holds%20that,layman%20attempts%20to%20administer%20it.)" stating that this doctrine is to be held definitively (see above, chapter XVIII, 2)*,* so that neither deacons nor lay people can exercise this ministry. Any attempt by them to do so would constitute simulation of the sacrament.

The fact of priestly ordination is sufficient in itself, and no extra "faculty" is required as with penance. The sacrament is valid even if the priest is excommunicated.

The conditions for lawfulness are not very strict, given the nature of the sacrament: it is principally the responsibility of the priest to whom has been committed the care of souls, but any other priest can administer the sacrament for a reasonable cause if he has the consent, at least presumed, of the aforementioned priest (canon 1003 §2[^540]).

**4. Those to whom the sacrament may be given**

The person to be anointed should have **attained the use of reason** (even if he or she lacks it at the time of the anointing); should **begin to be in danger by reason of illness or old age** (this does not mean the person has to be on point of death, but there should be "danger"); and should have the **intention** of receiving the sacrament (it should therefore be administered to those who, when in possession of their faculties, requested it at least implicitly).

> The wish to receive the sacrament is normally presumed in a baptised Catholic, but the presumption could be rebutted: see canon 1007[^541].
>
> In cases of doubt as to use of reason, the dangerous nature of the illness, or death, the sacrament is to be administered (canon 1005[^542]).
>
> The sacrament may be repeated if the person recovers and falls ill again, or if the danger in the same illness becomes more serious (canon 1004[^543]).
>
> Reception of the sacrament requires, in principle, the state of grace. Hence it should be preceded where possible by penance.

? QUESTIONS

1\. When is the sacrament of anointing of the sick to be administered?

2\. What considerations should be borne in mind in preparing to receive or administer the sacrament?

**\**
**CHAPTER XXVI:\
THE SACRAMENT OF ORDER\**

> READINGS FOR THIS CHAPTER
>
> [Code of Canon Law](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1dBfZuE0O4NTYPiaEdeUtdegdSEyK5YQM/view): Book IV, canons 1008-1054.
>
> Pius XII, Constitution [*Sacramentum Ordinis*](https://www.papalencyclicals.net/pius12/p12sacrao.htm), 30 November 1947.
>
> Vatican II, Dogmatic Constitution on the Church [*Lumen Gentium*](https://www.vatican.va/archive/hist_councils/ii_vatican_council/documents/vat-ii_const_19641121_lumen-gentium_en.html), 21 November 1964, nos. 26, 29.
>
> Paul VI, Apostolic Letter *motu proprio* [*Ministeria Quaedam*](https://www.ewtn.com/catholicism/library/ministeria-quaedam-9006), 15 August 1972.
>
> Sacred Congregation for the Doctrine of the Faith, Declaration [*Inter Insigniores*](https://www.vatican.va/roman_curia/congregations/cfaith/documents/rc_con_cfaith_doc_19761015_inter-insigniores_en.html), 15 October 1976.
>
> John Paul II, Apostolic Letter [*Ecclesia Dei*](https://www.vatican.va/roman_curia/pontifical_commissions/ecclsdei/documents/hf_jp-ii_motu-proprio_02071988_ecclesia-dei_en.html), 2 July 1988.
>
> John Paul II, Apostolic Letter [*Mulieris Dignitatem*](https://www.vatican.va/content/john-paul-ii/en/apost_letters/1988/documents/hf_jp-ii_apl_19880815_mulieris-dignitatem.html), 15 August 1988.
>
> [*Catechism of the Catholic Church*](https://www.vatican.va/archive/ENG0015/__P4S.HTM), nos. 1536-1538, 1554-1571, 1575-1589.
>
> John Paul II, Apostolic Letter [*Ordinatio Sacerdotalis*](https://www.vatican.va/content/john-paul-ii/en/apost_letters/1994/documents/hf_jp-ii_apl_19940522_ordinatio-sacerdotalis.html), 22 May 1994.
>
> Congregation for Catholic Education, [*Instruction concerning the criteria for the discernment of vocations with regard to persons with homosexual tendencies in view of their admission to the Seminary and to Holy Orders*](https://www.vatican.va/roman_curia/congregations/ccatheduc/documents/rc_con_ccatheduc_doc_20051104_istruzione_en.html), 4 November 2005.
>
> Benedict XVI, Apostolic Letter *motu proprio [Omnium in Mentem](https://www.vatican.va/content/benedict-xvi/en/apost_letters/documents/hf_ben-xvi_apl_20091026_codex-iuris-canonici.html)*, 26 October 2009.

**1. Nature and effects of the sacrament**

> See the [*Catechism of the Catholic Church*](https://www.vatican.va/archive/ENG0015/__P4Y.HTM), nos. 1581-1589.

Canon 1008 §1 states: "By divine institution, some of the Christian faithful are marked with an indelible character and constituted as sacred ministers by the sacrament of holy orders. They are thus consecrated and deputed so that, each according to his own grade, they may serve the People of God by a new and specific title." (revised wording following the amendments set out in Benedict XVI's Apostolic Letter *motu proprio [Omnium in Mentem](https://www.vatican.va/content/benedict-xvi/en/apost_letters/documents/hf_ben-xvi_apl_20091026_codex-iuris-canonici.html)*, 26 October 2009).

**2. Orders and ministries**

> See canons 1008-1009[^544]; the [*Catechism of the Catholic Church*](https://www.vatican.va/archive/ENG0015/__P4S.HTM), nos. 1537-1538 on the meaning of the word "orders"; and nos. 1554-1571 on the different degrees of order.

Canon 1009 specifies (§1) that "The orders are the episcopate, the priesthood and the diaconate", which "are conferred by the imposition of hands and the prayer of consecration which the liturgical books prescribe for each grade" (§2).

> The question of the matter and form of the sacrament was resolved by Pius XII in the Constitution [*Sacramentum Ordinis*](https://www.papalencyclicals.net/pius12/p12sacrao.htm), 30 November 1947. These consist of the laying on of hands and the prayer of consecration in accordance with the liturgical books.

[*Omnium in Mentem*](https://www.vatican.va/content/benedict-xvi/en/apost_letters/documents/hf_ben-xvi_apl_20091026_codex-iuris-canonici.html), "in order better to convey the teaching on deacons found in the Dogmatic Constitution *[Lumen Gentium](http://www.vatican.va/archive/hist_councils/ii_vatican_council/documents/vat-ii_const_19641121_lumen-gentium_en.html)* of the [Second Vatican Council](http://www.vatican.va/archive/hist_councils/ii_vatican_council/index.htm) (no. 29)", adds a third paragraph to canon 1009: "Those who are constituted in the order of the episcopate or the presbyterate receive the mission and capacity to act in the person of Christ the Head, whereas deacons are empowered to serve the People of God in the ministries of the liturgy, the word and charity."

> The 1917 Code listed 7 orders: priesthood, diaconate, subdiaconate, acolyte, exorcist, lector and porter. No reference was made to the episcopate as a special degree of the sacrament of orders; nor did that Code use the expression "episcopal ordination", but rather "episcopal consecration". The Dogmatic Constitution [*Lumen Gentium*](http://www.vatican.va/archive/hist_councils/ii_vatican_council/documents/vat-ii_const_19641121_lumen-gentium_en.html), no. 26, has clarified that the bishop is "invested with the fullness of the sacrament of Orders", so that the episcopate is now regarded as the highest degree of the sacrament.
>
> The *motu proprio [Ministeria Quaedam](https://www.ewtn.com/catholicism/library/ministeria-quaedam-9006)* (15 August 1972) suppressed the orders of porter, lector, exorcist, acolyte and subdeacon. These were merged into the functions of lector and acolyte, but were no longer considered degrees of the sacrament of order, but rather *ministries*, which can be entrusted to laymen. Their conferral is no longer termed "ordination" but "installation".

Deacons are not priests but ministers (see [*Lumen Gentium*](http://www.vatican.va/archive/hist_councils/ii_vatican_council/documents/vat-ii_const_19641121_lumen-gentium_en.html), no. 29, which is reflected in the revised wording of canon 1009 §3 as shown above). Although there are certain functions that are proper to deacons, these may also be discharged by a lay person in case of necessity; some of them may be discharged ordinarily by the acolyte or lector.

> On the question of permanent deacons, the [*Catechism of the Catholic Church*](https://www.vatican.va/archive/ENG0015/__P4U.HTM), no. 1571, states: "Since the Second Vatican Council the Latin Church has restored the diaconate 'as a proper and permanent rank of the hierarchy', while the Churches of the East had always maintained it. This permanent diaconate, which can be conferred on married men, constitutes an important enrichment for the Church's mission. Indeed it is appropriate and useful that men who carry out a truly diaconal ministry in the Church, whether in its liturgical and pastoral life or whether in its social and charitable works, should 'be strengthened by the imposition of hands which has come down from the apostles. They would be more closely bound to the altar and their ministry would be made more fruitful through the sacramental grace of the diaconate' (Vatican II, Decree [*Ad Gentes*](https://www.vatican.va/archive/hist_councils/ii_vatican_council/documents/vat-ii_decree_19651207_ad-gentes_en.html), 16 §6)."

**3. The minister of episcopal consecration**

Canon 1012[^545] states that the minister of sacred ordination is a consecrated bishop. Canon 1013[^546] lays down that the faculty to authorise episcopal ordination is reserved to the Roman Pontiff. This reservation does not affect the validity of the ordination, but its lawfulness.

> Canon 1387[^547] establishes the penalty for ordaining or being ordained a bishop without a Papal mandate. It was for such an offence that Archbishop Marcel Lefebvre was excommunicated in 1988, together with the four priests of the Priestly Fraternity of Pius X whom Archbishop Lefebvre ordained as bishops: see the Apostolic Letter [*Ecclesia Dei*](https://www.vatican.va/roman_curia/pontifical_commissions/ecclsdei/documents/hf_jp-ii_motu-proprio_02071988_ecclesia-dei_en.html) issued by Pope John Paul II on 2 July 1988.

As a sign of episcopal collegiality, it is normally a requirement for lawfulness that two other consecrating bishops should accompany the principal consecrating bishop. It is also fitting that all the bishops present should join them (canon 1014[^548]).

**4. The minister of ordination of deacons or priests**

> See the [*Catechism of the Catholic Church*](https://www.vatican.va/archive/ENG0015/__P4W.HTM), nos. 1575-1576.

Canon 1015 §1 states: "Each candidate is to be ordained to the priesthood or to the diaconate by his proper bishop, or with lawful dimissorial letters granted by that bishop." This provision, which affects the lawfulness of the ordination, is connected with the question of incardination (see above, chapter XIV, 2).

> The succeeding canons determine who is the proper bishop and who may give dimissorial letters, which are the authorisation required from the proper bishop when a different bishop is ordaining.

**5. Requirements on the part of those to be ordained**

> See canons 1024-1049[^549]; [*Catechism of the Catholic Church*](https://www.vatican.va/archive/ENG0015/__P4X.HTM), no. 1577.

The two objective requirements for ordination are that the person be male, and baptised (see canon 1024).

> On the question of women priests, see the Sacred Congregation for the Doctrine of the Faith's Declaration [*Inter Insigniores*](https://www.vatican.va/roman_curia/congregations/cfaith/documents/rc_con_cfaith_doc_19761015_inter-insigniores_en.html), 15 October 1976, and John Paul II's Apostolic Letters [*Mulieris Dignitatem*](https://www.vatican.va/content/john-paul-ii/en/apost_letters/1988/documents/hf_jp-ii_apl_19880815_mulieris-dignitatem.html), 15 August 1988, and [*Ordinatio Sacerdotalis*](https://www.vatican.va/content/john-paul-ii/en/apost_letters/1994/documents/hf_jp-ii_apl_19940522_ordinatio-sacerdotalis.html), 22 May 1994. In the latter document the Pope declared that the Church has no authority whatsoever to confer priestly ordination on women "and that this judgement is to be definitively held by all the Church's faithful".
>
> On 28 October 1995 the Congregation for the Doctrine of the Faith, replying to a question about the teaching contained in [*Ordinatio Sacerdotalis*](https://www.vatican.va/content/john-paul-ii/en/apost_letters/1994/documents/hf_jp-ii_apl_19940522_ordinatio-sacerdotalis.html), declared that it belonged to the deposit of faith. On 19 December 2007 the same Congregation established a *latae sententiae* excommunication reserved to the Apostolic See for anyone attempting to ordain a woman, or for any woman attempting to be ordained (now incorporated into the Code in canon 1379 §3[^550]).

For the lawfulness of the ordination of a priest or deacon, canon 1025 gives a series of requirements, including that the person to be ordained should be considered beneficial to the ministry of the Church.

> In addition, he must be free (canon 1026), and have adequate formation (canon 1027) and knowledge regarding the order itself and its obligations (canon 1028). Canon 1029 provides a list of the signs by which a divine vocation can be canonically proven. The minimum ages for ordination are set out in canons 1031 (for deacons and priests) and 378 (for bishops). Other prerequisites for ordination are given in canons 1033-1039.
>
> Impediments -- whether temporary ("simple impediments") or permanent ("irregularities") -- to receiving or exercising holy orders are dealt with in canons 1040-1049.
>
> An [Instruction](https://www.vatican.va/roman_curia/congregations/ccatheduc/documents/rc_con_ccatheduc_doc_20051104_istruzione_en.html) of the Congregation for Catholic Education issued on 4 November 2005 sets out the criteria to be applied in respect of the admittance of persons with homosexual tendencies to seminaries or to holy orders.

It should be borne in mind that it is the relevant Church authority that ultimately decides on the suitability of a candidate. The candidate himself has no right as such to sacred orders; although to avoid arbitrary actions on the part of the authority, the possibility exists of a hierarchical recourse against the decision to refuse ordination (see chapter XXXI on the Protection of Rights in the Church).

? QUESTIONS

1\. What is the difference between orders and ministries in the Church?

2\. What are the fundamental requirements on the part of a person to be ordained?

**CHAPTER XXVII:\
THE SACRAMENT OF MARRIAGE\**
